decisions.title: Secrets are held behind a handle the door swaps for the credential
decisions.context: Agents need to use credentials without ever holding them, and revoking access must be instant even for a static key.
decisions.decision: A seat holds a short-lived handle bound to its identity. The real credential sits in the door's encrypted store and never leaves the server. The door's proxy checks SpiceDB, swaps the handle for the credential, forwards the call and writes one audit line. Built in Rust inside the door; no OpenBao unless credentials minted on demand are later needed.
decisions.quote: use something with the service, like a temporary key, and that is then mapped so the actual credential can be used.
consequences: Revoking is dropping the handle, instant for a static key too.
The real key is rotated upstream only when it is suspected leaked.
A key that cannot rotate is still used through the proxy and never read.

decisions.title: The token revolver is the first consumer of the handle
decisions.context: The workers that run Claude sessions and builders walk their own ordered list of accounts when a session prints its usage-limit words.
decisions.decision: The worker asks the broker for its next account instead of walking its own list; the store keeps the set of real accounts behind one handle and the proxy takes the next in turn and logs which one served each call. This replaces the account pool file.
decisions.quote: that's exactly the kind of thing that we'd want to plug into this, to be able to draw in from there
consequences: Usage is attributed in one place.
Resting an account is a change in the store, with no file copied to any machine.

decisions.title: Everything is pegged to a human authority
decisions.context: Agents are provisioned under people and act with delegated access.
decisions.decision: A person signs in first; an agent is provisioned under that person with its own identity; the person's permissions are the ceiling and the agent holds an explicit subset; every grant says who may exercise it and who may pass it on; withdrawing the authority stops every grant derived from it. The exact delegation schema is not settled by this decision.
decisions.quote: Basically everything needs to be pegged against the human's base permissions.
consequences: A handle is issued only under a grant that traces to a person.

decisions.title: Manifold is optional and every project stands alone
decisions.context: The statement names seats being started and ended.
decisions.decision: The engine that starts or ends a seat is whichever one runs the agent: manifold, aion, or a customer's own. Each project in the stack works without the others; an engine without the broker reads its own pool file as it does today.
decisions.quote: It's in the stack as an optional execution engine, but it's not mandatory... I don't want anybody really planning it as a structural cog.
consequences: No broker requirement depends on manifold being present.

decisions.title: The identity database is PostgreSQL, possibly on a network device
decisions.context: At 14:08 in the Dot room Tom said he had hoped to get rid of PostgreSQL, and asked whether the team thought it was the best solution. The working team decision was one PostgreSQL service and one database for Rauthy and SpiceDB, with separate roles and schema namespaces.
decisions.decision: PostgreSQL is used for the identity product's database. It may be set up on one of the network devices rather than on Tom's Mac.
decisions.quote: Yeah, so we can use Postgres, that's fine. We might just set it up on one of the network devices so it doesn't have to run here.
consequences: Row 02's one PostgreSQL service and database stands.
The host is not assumed to be Tom's Mac; the deployment names its database address as configuration.

decisions.title: A role changes only by a deliberate, explicit act
decisions.context: Version 4 of the identity mock-up gave roles a builder. At 18:54 on 23 September the room asked Tom whether editing a role changes every holder at once or leaves each holder with the copy made when they got it.
decisions.decision: Editing a role makes a new version of it, and a holder never changes version silently as a side effect of the edit. A holder moves between versions either by a deliberate, recorded act or by an explicit rule shown in advance to the person the holder answers to, such as a move at the holding's next renewal. Which of the two is the default is open. A provisional role is a role held under a grant with an end date: when the date passes the holding lapses, and nothing renews it unless someone grants it again.
decisions.quote: whichever way you went, you'd want it to be deliberate, … and if not deliberate, then explicit … their old lease expires and they don't get a new one
consequences: The role screen shows which version each holder is on, and who still holds an older one.
A holding's end date belongs to its grant, not to the role version: a version change never extends a provisional holding.
A lapsed provisional holding leaves the audit record of its end, and the grants it carried stop at the next check.
Whether a role is a live group or a template copied at grant time stays open.

decisions.title: The product starts an agent by giving its start command, never by running it
decisions.context: On 22 September Tom settled that the product owns an agent's lifecycle as its record and decision, with a runtime carrying it out (ADR-004). On 23 September at 18:56 he asked how a person actually starts a new agent from it.
decisions.decision: The product is not an execution engine. For the first release an agent's file gives the command that starts it on a chosen machine: the command carries the agent's identity and its handles, never a credential's value, and it is rendered from the agent's kept launch record. A started agent reports back, so the sessions screen shows what is running. A terminal inside the product, sandboxes, virtual machines and containers are later runtimes that plug in, and none is built into this product.
decisions.quote: I don't want this to become like an execution kind of engine … in the first instance, it's starting out with basically like, cool, here's the command that you need to start Waffles
consequences: Every agent carries a launch record: the machine, the runtime, the program, its arguments, the working directory and the handles it needs, by name.

A session is shown running only after the agent reports its start, signed with its own key and naming its launch record; a report that is not authenticated as that identity and that launch record is refused. Copying the command is not a start.
A session that never reports stays unconfirmed.

decisions.title: An agent's file shows its lys certificate
decisions.context: Reviewing version 4 of the identity mock-up at 18:55 on 23 September, Tom asked that the lys certificate and receipt work be part of the product.
decisions.decision: An agent's file shows its lys certificate once one is issued: what it claims, who signed it, when it was issued and when it expires, with the signed receipts of the changes made to it. An agent registered before any key or proof of possession was supplied shows its certificate as not issued, never a placeholder.
decisions.quote: just making sure that sort of like the original lys certificating stuff is in there
consequences: A change to its grants or role version issues a new certificate; the old one is withdrawn in the log, never edited.
Anyone can verify the certificate and its inclusion in the log offline with standard tools.
Production keys and receipts outside tests remain Tom's acts.
The conformance list checks that a registered agent's certificate, or its not-issued state, and its receipts can be read from its file.

decisions.title: People sign in through a maintained Rauthy fork of our own
decisions.decided_by: Tom (the fork, 14:35 to 14:42); Waffles (its branch and upgrade rule, 15:30:50)
decisions.context: Rauthy v0.36.2 refuses a second provider for a user ('user is already federated'), so linking Google and GitHub to one person needs a change Rauthy upstream is unlikely to accept. Sources: docs/design/identity/STATEMENT-2026-09-22.md:191 (Decided 14:35, Tom); IDENTITY-001 authority (docs/design/identity/briefs/IDENTITY-001.json:10, Tom 14:35 to 14:42; docs/design/identity/briefs/IDENTITY-001.json:17, Waffles 15:30:50) and review_decisions (docs/design/identity/briefs/IDENTITY-001.json:35).
decisions.decision: Rauthy authenticates people, and its one-provider-per-user limit is changed in a fork we maintain, ablative-io/rauthy, not contributed upstream as a prerequisite. The maintained branch is ablative, created from upstream v0.36.2 commit dd61ac3c84d6b238108dc8438b53043b5177a662; the fork's main stays an untouched upstream mirror; lys pins an exact commit of ablative as the submodule vendor/rauthy. Upgrades rebase ablative onto upstream release tags only, each in its own gated row; no cherry-picks and no reset of main.
decisions.quote: The platform keeps its own maintained fork of Rauthy rather than depending on an upstream contribution.
consequences: The fork carries its security fixes for as long as it lives: its maintenance owner is Chippy, with Waffles reviewing security and update decisions (docs/design/identity/RAUTHY-BASELINE.md:39), and the release-and-advisory check recurs before every install (docs/design/identity/STATEMENT-2026-09-22.md:177).
Real sign-in waits on a rebase onto an upstream release carrying both hardening commits, the separate future brief IDENTITY-002 (docs/design/identity/briefs/IDENTITY-001.json:462-473).
A change inside the fork belongs to the fork's own repository: a brief of this repository names such a file with its owner and never lists it as its own file.

decisions.title: Every product shares one design and keeps its own accent; the identity product's is orange
decisions.decided_by: Tom (15:18, 15:20 and 15:21:43), relayed by Waffles (15:19 and 15:21)
decisions.context: Tom asked for a consistent design across the products and named Aion's browser appearance as the one he is happiest with; Cambium is not yet the reference. Sources: docs/design/identity/STATEMENT-2026-09-22.md:194; IDENTITY-001 authority (docs/design/identity/briefs/IDENTITY-001.json:14-15) and review_decisions (docs/design/identity/briefs/IDENTITY-001.json:43-44).
decisions.decision: The identity screens follow Aion's structure, typography, spacing and interaction, and Rauthy's client themes take the same colours, with no build dependency on Cambium or Aion. Each product keeps its own accent within the estate colour family: Cambium green, Aion blue and black, Argus light blue, Haematite mustard. The identity product's accent is orange (accent #D4975A, deep #A86B2E, wash #3D2A17 in the estate colour tokens), set apart from Manifold's copper. No product is silently made Aion-blue, and purple is not used.
decisions.quote: Every product shares one design and keeps its own accent.
consequences: Rauthy's pages carry our colours and corner radius only; their fonts and layout stay upstream's (docs/design/identity/STATEMENT-2026-09-22.md:191).
Exact accessible light and dark accent values are declared and reviewed before a theme is accepted.
Whether one design system is extracted for every product is not settled by this decision.

decisions.title: An identity is registered, active, suspended or retired
decisions.decided_by: Archie, for the working team (proposal of 17:10); not ruled by Tom
decisions.context: Tom, 17:08, put identity, access, permissions and the start of lifecycle management before everything else (docs/design/identity/STATEMENT-2026-09-22.md:183). Archie proposed these states so the directory has something to register an identity into; the document calls itself 'a proposal for the room, not a settled design' (docs/design/identity/LIFECYCLE-STATES-2026-09-22.md:1-8).
decisions.decision: An identity is in one of four states: registered (exists in the directory, no grants, no credential handle, may not act), active (may act within its grants), suspended (kept whole, grants kept but not effective) and retired (permanent, history kept, never reactivated; a new identity is made instead). Register, activate, suspend, reinstate and retire are the only transitions, each one signed audit record naming the authenticated actor and their provenance, the identity, from, to, when and reason. Having a grant or a credential is a fact beside the state, not a state. A person is registered by first sign-in; an agent is registered by a signed-in person, who carries it as its responsible person for life and may cause every transition of their own agents. Source: docs/design/identity/LIFECYCLE-STATES-2026-09-22.md:17-44 and docs/design/identity/LIFECYCLE-STATES-2026-09-22.md:71-95.
decisions.quote: We got to talk about identity access management, permissions, and the start of lifecycle management before we get to the nitty gritty of the lifecycle that we're actually managing
consequences: DIRECTORY-003 records the state beside each identity; no check reads it until the permission work of road step 2.

The room's own questions stay with the proposal: whether a reason is mandatory on suspend and retire, and whether activation needs a credential handle (docs/design/identity/LIFECYCLE-STATES-2026-09-22.md:101-103).

decisions.title: The home reaches a harness through a preset launch template per harness, never a transcript converter
decisions.decided_by: Tom, ruling of 16:00 on 22 September 2026, filed by Archie at 06:15 on 26 September 2026; the ruling was not held in the tree before this entry
decisions.context: A home holds the pieces a new session is made from (the record, the canon and the handover) but nothing turned them into a running session on a harness. The closest written form of the rule was stage 2 of docs/design/identity/CONTEXT-ROADMAP-2026-09-22.md (command templates map a home onto a harness, substitutions are data, a missing required input fails); the 16:00 ruling itself was recorded nowhere in docs/ until HOME-002 was filed on it.
decisions.decision: The home keeps one preset template per harness that maps the pieces onto that harness: the MCP configuration, the environment variables, which secrets the session may read and which it may only use through a handle, what is appended to the system prompt, and where the prior conversation goes, delivered as files and runtime variables with command mappings in text. The rejected road is a transcript converter that translates one harness's conversation into another's: the prior conversation reaches a harness only as that harness's own file, rendered from the record and resumed by the harness's own means.
consequences: Each harness gets its own template and its own measurement; there is no generic launch core, and a template names how its harness fills the transcript slot.
A template names its slots; a slot it does not know is refused by name, so a new slot (the canon, the handover) is a new template version.
A secret appears in a template and in every rendered file only as its handle; filling a readable secret's value belongs to the secrets rows (ADR-001).
Every render of a template is recorded on the session with the template hash and the session head hash, so a stranger can tell which template a session was launched with.
The launch line is given, never run (ADR-007).
